Longer training, imitating human logs, and human-log speed targets yield either no measurable gain or adverse effects. Without further training, Lao Siji also places among the leaders on HUGSIM and Odyssey. The final training takes only one GPU-hour and shifts the weights by 3.9% from the shipped model. Code will be released after review.

Computer Vision.title: Navi-Agent: Unlocalized Monocular Navigation Agent
Computer Vision.summary: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires an embodied agent to execute long-horizon instructions in unknown environments. Existing zero-shot VLN-CE systems typically maintain spatial states through geometric localization or coordinate-based representations. Recent geometry-constrained navigation removes depth and globally consistent coordinates, but maintaining persistent spatial awareness for place confirmation, progress verification, and recovery remains challenging. We present Navi-Agent, a zero-shot VLN-CE agent that constructs a coordinate-free spatial state from visual observations and executed motion histories. Navi-Agent organizes this state as a navigation topology, where nodes represent visual places and edges represent motion transitions. This representation enables observation-based approximate self-localization, task progress verification, and visual revisitation-based recovery. Navi-Agent performs closed-loop navigation by decomposing instructions into sub-goals, executing local visual navigation, and verifying visited places through the constructed spatial state. Experiments on zero-shot VLN-CE benchmark and real-world robot platforms show that Navi-Agent achieves state-of-the-art performance among geometry-constrained methods while remaining competitive with approaches relying on geometric localization.

Computer Vision.title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
Computer Vision.summary: Predicting 6-DoF grasp poses from a single RGB-D frame has recently achieved impressive accuracy, yet performance can degrade significantly when the target object is heavily occluded by clutter. In this paper, we establish TARGO, the first benchmark dataset for TARget-driven Grasping under Occlusions, and introduce TARGO-Net, a grasp prediction model designed for visual occlusion. Our main contributions are fourfold: 1) We identify the visual occlusion challenge in single-view RGB-D 6-DoF grasping and show that current state-of-the-art models still suffer under severe occlusion. 2) We propose the TARGO dataset, which supports training and testing 6-DoF grasp models across different visual occlusion levels and enables robustness evaluation in real-world scenarios. 3) We devise TARGO-Net, a transformer-based grasping model with a target completion module and target-scene cross-attention, which achieves the most robust performance across all visual occlusion levels. 4) We show that target completion, number of occluders, and target minimum dimension also relate to grasp success in addition to visual occlusion.
Computer Vision.comment: Published at International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV), 2026

Computer Vision.title: Remember, Replay, Adapt: Learning from Past Experience in Online Vision-and-Language Navigation
Computer Vision.summary: Existing feedback-based methods for online vision-and-language navigation (VLN) primarily learn from current episode outcomes, leaving previously acquired feedback underutilized. Inspired by human episodic memory, we propose R2A, an online VLN adaptation framework that continually reuses successful and failed navigation experiences for policy learning. Specifically, Success-Failure Memory (SFM) retains successful and failed navigation episodes with acquired feedback and retrieves task-relevant experiences based on incoming instructions, enabling historical feedback to guide subsequent navigation. Prior-Anchored Adaptation (PAA) learns from these experiences by reinforcing successful trajectories and suppressing failed ones relative to a frozen pretrained policy, while regularizing behavioral drift. Together, these modules enable continual feedback reuse and stable policy adaptation without source-domain data or expert supervision. Extensive experiments across three benchmarks, REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE, and five navigation backbones demonstrate consistent performance gains. On the REVERIE validation unseen split, R2A improves DUET's SR from 46.98% to 69.84% and SPL from 33.73% to 50.98%.

Computer Vision.title: Illusion of Explainability: A Sanity Check for Spectral Band Attribution in Satellite Time-Series Crop Classification
Computer Vision.summary: Attribution methods are commonly validated through convergence across methods and consistency with domain knowledge, yet neither criterion establishes whether identified features are necessary for a task. This limitation is particularly relevant in multispectral remote sensing, where overlapping spectral information makes individual bands potentially substitutable. We investigate this gap in crop-type classification using GradientSHAP, Shapley sampling, and Occlusion on a U-TAE segmentation model trained on Sentinel-2 time series from the PASTIS benchmark. All three methods identify vegetation-sensitive spectral regions consistent with domain knowledge, while Shapley and Occlusion exhibit strong ordering sensitivity in deletion and insertion tests. However, these properties do not reliably predict retraining performance. Aggregate attribution consensus masks substantial per-class disagreement, with pairwise mean Spearman correlations ranging from 0.09 to 0.79. Models retrained from scratch using the five lowest-ranked bands perform comparably to or better than those using the five highest-ranked bands. Furthermore, attribution rankings from an independently trained model with identical configuration and seed identify a different top-five subset that yields better retraining performance. Analysis of all 252 five-band subsets reveals consistently low effective dimensionality (1.35 to 2.62), suggesting substantial spectral redundancy. These findings demonstrate that plausible and apparently faithful attribution rankings do not necessarily identify task-relevant bands for improved retrained performance, highlighting the limitations of band-level feature attribution in spectrally redundant input spaces.
Computer Vision.comment: Accepted at the 4th Computer Vision for Earth Observation (CV4EO) Workshop at WACV 2027

Computer Vision.title: TRUCO: A Scalable Lock-Free Algorithm for Parallel Contour Extraction
Computer Vision.summary: Extracting binary contours and their containment hierarchy is a fundamental step in many computer vision pipelines. While the standard Suzuki--Abe algorithm is inherently sequential, existing parallel tracers neither preserve its exact contours nor compute their hierarchy. This paper presents TRUCO (Threaded Raster Unrestricted Contour Ownership), a lock-free parallel algorithm for multi-core CPUs that produces the exact output of Suzuki--Abe. TRUCO relies on two core ideas. First, the image is partitioned into horizontal stripes, and a geometric ownership rule allows each thread to trace complete contours independently across stripe boundaries, avoiding both locks and post-processing merges. Second, contour tracing is decoupled from hierarchy reconstruction, which is performed in a subsequent parallel pass and can be skipped entirely when only the contours are needed. We formally prove that TRUCO is deterministic, data-race-free, and identical in output to Suzuki--Abe regardless of thread count. Across diverse high-resolution datasets-from sparse segmentation masks to dense real-world photographs-TRUCO achieves speedups of 4.7x to 17.4x over the fastest sequential baseline with hierarchy computation, and 2.3x to 17.8x without it.

Computer Vision.title: EvoKnow: Continual Knowledge Evolution for AI-Generated Image Detection
Computer Vision.summary: AI-generated image detectors are commonly trained on fixed generator domains and become difficult to maintain as new generative models emerge. Continual adaptation is challenging because replaying historical generated images is costly, whereas updating shared parameters with limited current-domain data can overwrite prior forensic knowledge. We propose EvoKnow, a replay-free framework that formulates continual AI-generated image detection as forensic knowledge evolution. EvoKnow preserves a shared forensic basis learned from base domains, incrementally adds isolated residual experts for complementary generator-relevant evidence, and retrieves expertise through an Analytical Incremental Router (AIR) updated in closed form from current-stage generated images and accumulated sufficient statistics. Experiments demonstrate effective cross-generator generalization, few-shot expansion, and long-horizon continual adaptation. With ten generated images per arriving generator, EvoKnow achieves 96.70% average accuracy on non-base GenImage generators and 94.48% accuracy on Chameleon without target-benchmark adaptation. Under a strict replay-free continual learning protocol, EvoKnow achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance, attaining 96.32% mean stage-wise accuracy and 4.32% average forgetting.

Computer Vision.title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
Computer Vision.summary: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

Computer Vision.title: TwinPast: Benchmarking Historical Evidence Use in Streaming Video Understanding with Evidence Contrastive Video Pairs
Computer Vision.summary: High accuracy on streaming video benchmarks does not show that a model uses visual history. Auditing OVO-Bench and StreamingBench, we find that recent frames alone suffice for 32% of sampled historical-task questions, and that the question and options alone also yield many correct answers. We introduce TwinPast, a benchmark of 350 human-reviewed video pairs spanning five historical tasks. The two videos in a pair share the recent video context, question, and ordered options, and differ in earlier events and therefore in the correct answer. Each video is evaluated independently and PairAcc requires both answers to be correct, so an answer determined by the shared inputs cannot solve a pair. Masking the annotated critical evidence lowers PairAcc from as high as 91% to at most 19%, whereas equal-area masking elsewhere changes it by at most 3.4 points. The strongest streaming system reaches 49% PairAcc, while general-purpose MLLMs given each complete video reach 67-91%, leaving substantial headroom. Streaming systems fail mainly by giving both histories the same answer. They give different valid answers on at most 57% of pairs, while the general-purpose MLLMs do so on 79-94%. Case studies further show wrong answers when the deciding evidence is still available at the final query.

Computer Vision.title: AGPF: Dynamic Source Selection for Feature Pyramid Fusion
Computer Vision.summary: Feature pyramids provide dense predictors with features at several spatial resolutions. However, it remains largely unexplored which pyramid levels each output location should aggregate information from. We investigate this question by allowing each output location to attend to features from every pyramid level and measuring how attention is distributed across scales. Surprisingly, locations on the finest output grid allocate approximately 75\% of their attention to features two levels coarser, rather than to the current or adjacent levels. Even on the same output grid, the balance shifts toward coarser features as object size increases. These observations motivate Asymmetric Global Pyramid Fusion (AGPF), a neck that preserves the original output grids while allowing each location to dynamically select its contextual sources across scales. Each location interacts with a multiscale memory whose features are aligned in image coordinates, enabling flexible cross-scale aggregation without altering prediction resolutions. Compared with FPN, AGPF improves all 19 object detection and all seven instance segmentation configurations evaluated on COCO. A single fusion block improves Cascade Mask R-CNN by 1.7 box AP and 2.3 mask AP, and the gains consistently transfer to semantic and panoptic segmentation.

Computer Vision.title: Beyond Vehicle-Centric Data: Scaling Autonomous Driving through Roadside-to-Vehicle Generation
Computer Vision.summary: Training autonomous driving models requires large and diverse datasets, collected primarily by vehicles. Scaling them entails investment in fleet operation, data processing and annotation. Road infrastructure records traffic and multi-vehicle interactions, yet the viewpoint gap between roadside and onboard sensors limits its direct use for training. Here we introduce AnyR2V, a framework that transforms multimodal roadside observations into seven-camera surround-view videos for different vehicle perspectives. It aggregates sequential observations into a shared scene representation of geometry and road-user motion, then renders appearance, depth and layout conditions along target-vehicle trajectories. Supervised by spatiotemporally aligned roadside-vehicle pairs, AnyR2V generates surround-view videos guided by scene structure and road-user motion. Existing roadside 3D bounding boxes are transformed into target-vehicle coordinates and paired with generated images, allowing one traffic recording and its annotations to yield training data from multiple vehicle perspectives. We construct R2V360, a dataset of 89 real traffic sequences at an urban intersection, with aligned multimodal roadside data and onboard surround-view videos. AnyR2V outperforms six scene reconstruction methods in image fidelity and in depth and semantic agreement between generated and real onboard images. We further evaluate generated videos along other vehicles' trajectories by adding them to real training data. Adding generated frames equal to 50% of the original real training frame count improves mean average precision (mAP) by 3.3-3.4 AP-points across three 3D object detectors on the real onboard test set, relative to real-data-only baselines. These results demonstrate that roadside traffic records can provide training data from multiple vehicle perspectives, offering a new data source for autonomous driving.

Computer Vision.title: PRISM: Primitive-Integrated Separable Modulation with Priority Visual Memory Queue for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
Computer Vision.summary: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL) recognizes unseen attribute--object pairs by recombining primitives from seen compositions. Existing methods stop sharing evidence at deployment: fixed prototypes cannot exploit unlabeled test streams, while composition-wise refinement cannot propagate corrections across pairs sharing a primitive. We introduce PRISM, an online CZSL framework that extends primitive sharing to test-time adaptation. Its Hierarchical Knowledge Accumulation Module (HiKAM) factorizes prototype migration into composition-, attribute-, and object-level residual banks. A Priority Visual Memory Queue (PVMQ), initialized by Prototype Queue Initialization (PQI), grounds text updates with bounded visual evidence. The same adaptive core supports exhaustive Full PRISM and recall-calibrated Adaptive PRISM-Lite, which selects candidate budgets from held-out ranks. Comprehensive closed- and open-world experiments on UT-Zappos, MIT-States, and C-GQA demonstrate the state of the art, with Full PRISM achieving the best open-world AUC and harmonic mean on all three benchmarks and the best closed-world results on UT-Zappos and C-GQA. Fine-grained long-tail and non-stationary primitive-block evaluations reveal gains on under-supported concepts and stable adaptation under prolonged skew. Adaptive PRISM-Lite further delivers substantial efficiency gains in the full open-world space with only a small accuracy cost. PRISM thus combines primitive-shared online adaptation, multimodal grounding, and candidate-aware inference.

Computer Vision.title: When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?
Computer Vision.summary: We ask whether a compact universal multimodal embedding models can produce better search embeddings by running the same layers again. Looped transformers add computation with nearly unchanged model size, making them an appealing alternative to a larger encoder. Their success in language-model reasoning and recent use for retrieval motivate the idea, but higher retrieval scores alone do not reveal what an extra pass contributes. We study eleven loop designs and training variants on three checkpoints of one vision-language architecture. Our protocol distinguishes whether a model uses its extra pass, whether its image states respond to the query, and whether those updates improve retrieval. We prove that an image placed before the query remains query-independent through repeated layers when information only travels forward. We then open a query-to-image path in three ways, including order-alternating recurrence, which places the query first on the next pass. Each path produces query-sensitive image states. For bidirectional attention and order alternation, freezing later visual updates does not lower accuracy. On all 78 datasets of the Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark version 2 (MMEB-V2), a standard added loop loses 0.46 points against its trained control; an intermediate generative stage changes the effect to +0.36. A model pretrained with recurrence gains +4.23 points over its own loop-removed control and benefits from query-conditioned image updates when answering visual questions or locating objects from text.

Computer Vision.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
Computer Vision.summary: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictest level, locate exactly where they change. All 11 video world models we evaluate fall short. The best averages 18.3% pair accuracy over real and simulated scenes, below the 25% of random guessing. Models flip as often on steps that leave the future unchanged as on steps that change it, and their response stays flat across the sweeps. On the same frames, a vision-language model is selective and traces a near S-shaped curve near the boundary, and a coding agent that measures the image comes close to the true boundary. This implies that the deciding information is in the frame, and video models just miss it. We therefore urge the community to rethink world modeling as pure video prediction. Next-frame prediction must do more than draw plausible pixels; it must also identify the causal states that control future dynamics.

Computer Vision.title: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
Computer Vision.summary: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. Existing methods either re-inject vision at inference or train policies for stronger grounding, but where to intervene relies on perception heuristics rather than principled gain analysis, and how local visual influence propagates remains implicit. We study this problem from an information-theoretic standpoint and derive a lower bound on the downstream visual gain of a one-step intervention, which suggests two factors: local branching room (token entropy) and downstream visual propagation potential (suffix divergence from a vision-marginalized reference). Guided by this analysis, we propose reflection-anchor policy optimization (RAPO), a GRPO-based policy optimization method that selects high-entropy reflection anchors and optimizes a chain-masked finite-window KL surrogate for downstream visual dependence. Experiments on reasoning-intensive and general-domain benchmarks show that RAPO delivers substantial gains over strong baselines across multiple LVLM backbones. Mechanism analyses further indicate that reflection anchors are enriched for visually sensitive decision points and that RAPO increases contrastive visual-dependence signals along generated trajectories.

Computer Vision.title: Optical GeoAI and spatial modeling enable urban-canopy mapping and resilience screening in Davis, California
Computer Vision.summary: Timely urban-canopy information is essential for linking remote sensing with heat, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture Imagery Program imagery (0.6 m RGB+NIR). DeepForest generated crown candidates; an NDVI threshold, non-maximum suppression, and box-prompted Segment Anything Model (ViT-B) produced a crown-anchored canopy surface. Analyses used the 25.92 km2 Census TIGER municipal boundary and a 100 m grid. The workflow retained 11,741 candidate crowns and mapped 7.71 km2 of canopy (29.8% of the city). On the identical extent, pixel precision was 0.804, pixel recall was 0.873, and 97.4% of candidate centers agreed with the 2022 USDA/CAL FIRE LiDAR-assisted canopy product (IoU 0.719; Dice 0.837; area recovery 108.5%). Approximately 49% of candidates occurred within 15 m of a road. Canopy was inversely associated with Landsat land-surface temperature (Spearman rho = -0.477; partial rho = -0.551 controlling for built probability), and spatial-lag modeling confirmed clear neighborhood structure. Two transparent attention surfaces combined canopy need with thermal and contextual indicators. The framework provides a reproducible, updateable screening layer that complements structural canopy products and municipal inventories while retaining assumptions, data provenance, and spatial diagnostics for planning interpretation.
Computer Vision.comment: 17 pages, 10 figures + 5 supplementary figures, 7 tables. Revised preprint (expanded canopy infill; IoU 0.719). Preprint submitted to Frontiers. Code: https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/Davis_Urban_Canopy_GeoAI Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21925526

Computer Vision.title: MoRAE: Flow-Friendly Self-Supervised Latents for Text-to-Motion Generation
Computer Vision.summary: Which latent space should a text-to-motion generator model? We show that a self-supervised motion representation, once compressed, is a better generative space than latents learned by reconstruction. Our approach, MoRAE, is simple: we pre-train a Motion-JEPA encoder that predicts hidden joint trajectories from the rest of the body, and compress its frozen features into a compact latent for a standard flow transformer. Two observations drive this design. First, prediction yields features that capture action semantics and cross-joint structure better than reconstruction. Second, these features are ill-conditioned, and a standard flow transformer generates poorly in them directly. Compressing them into a compact latent makes generation reliable and places cross-joint structure on the directions the flow models most accurately. With a 58M DiT and the standard CLIP text condition, MoRAE achieves state-of-the-art FID on HumanML3D and KIT-ML while maintaining retrieval-based text consistency and diversity close to real motion.

Computer Vision.title: Attribution Gaps in Zero-Training LLM+OVOD Pipelines: A Fine-Grained Analysis of the CAAP--SNAP Discrepancy
Computer Vision.summary: LAOD and similar zero-training LLM+open-vocabulary-detector (OVOD) pipelines score two things separately: class-agnostic localization accuracy (CAAP) and semantic naming accuracy (SNAP). The two consistently diverge, and nobody has asked why. This paper asks why, on the full 5,000-image COCO-Val split (27,273 detections) rather than the small subset the original work evaluated on. Object visual complexity turns out not to be the driver -- small and occluded objects are, if anything, localized better than large ones. Vocabulary novelty is: once the LLM's wording falls outside the detector's native category set, localization accuracy falls from 80.9% to 31.6%. That drop is not spread evenly across unfamiliar phrasing, though. Almost all of it comes from cases where the novel wording actually names a different object than the one COCO annotated (true synonyms still score 89.3%; semantically unrelated "noise" labels score 12.0%). A closer look at a further failure subset tells a similar story: 78-88% of what looks like complete localization failure is really the model correctly finding a real object that COCO's non-exhaustive 80-category scheme simply never labeled, not hallucination. Swap the detector backbone (YOLO-World for Grounding DINO) or the LLM (Gemma-3 for Qwen2.5-VL) and both the effect and its rough size hold up, so this looks like a general property of the pipeline family rather than a quirk of one model pairing. The upshot is that a large share of the apparent CAAP--SNAP gap traces back to closed-category annotation limits rather than a real grounding failure, which matters for how we detect hallucination, analyze failure modes, and design evaluation for grounded multimodal systems meant to work in the open world.
Computer Vision.comment: v2: Corrected a corpus-level CAAP computation error in v1 (detections were matched against ground-truth boxes of all images); corrected value 0.21 vs 0.38 reported in v1. All dependent analyses recomputed; vocabulary classification bug also fixed. Code: github.com/hollis-png/laod-caap-snap-attribution

Computer Vision.title: Fine-Grained RLAIF for Visual Safety: Learning to Zoom into Hazards for Multimodal Safety Alignment
Computer Vision.summary: Recent multimodal safety alignment heavily relies on a text-centric paradigm, assuming risks are explicit in language or globally prominent in images. However, real-world hazards are often visually subtle or peripheral, causing existing models to fail due to their reliance on coarse, global visual representations. In this work, we study fine-grained visual safety alignment and introduce a challenging 1,200-sample benchmark across four domains, where hazards necessitate localized inspection. To address this, we propose Fine-Grained RLAIF (FGR), a reinforcement learning framework that casts image zoom-in as a learnable perception policy. FGR employs a decomposed reward design to jointly align three core safety behaviors: (i) where to look via a visual evidence reward, (ii) when to act via a tool-formatting constraint, and (iii) how to reason via visually grounded safety explanations. FGR achieves accuracy ranging from 86.71% to 93.00%, consistently outperforming strong multimodal and agent-based baselines.

Computer Vision.title: When Backdoors Can Be Switched Off: Suppression-Aware Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
Computer Vision.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map visual observations, robot states, and natural-language instructions to robotic actions, but their multimodal interfaces introduce new security risks. Existing VLA backdoor attacks primarily study trigger-based activation and stealthy action manipulation, leaving conditional suppression of malicious behavior underexplored. We investigate suppression-aware backdoors, which combine conjunctive trigger activation with instruction-conditioned suppression. We instantiate this design through three variants: Cross-Modal Trigger, combining robot-state and spatially separated visual triggers; Self-Suppressing Trigger, requiring a state trigger and a [DISRUPT] instruction token for activation, with [RESTORE] token suppressing the attack; and Multi-Trigger, additionally requiring a visual trigger while retaining suppression even when physical triggers persist. We evaluate these attacks using SmolVLA on two SO-100 manipulation datasets against four baselines: State Backdoor, BadVLA, TabVLA, and SilentDrift. Self-Suppressing and Multi-Trigger reduce Isolation Forest detection from 96--98% to 1--18% and action-space l divergence by 10--14X, achieving 63--71% attack success rates with perfect clean-task performance. Experiments with OpenVLA on LIBERO further show that the attacks transfer to a 7B-parameter policy, evading STRIP and action-distribution-shift detection. Our findings establish conditional suppression as an important dimension for evaluating backdoor threats in VLA policies.

Computer Vision.title: SemLite-GS: Semantic-Selective Parallel Gaussian Splatting for Lightweight Building Reconstruction from UAV Oblique Imagery
Computer Vision.summary: Lightweight 3D building models support urban spatial analysis, but their production often requires dense scene reconstruction, building extraction, and mesh simplification. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is more efficient than conventional multi-view stereo, existing large-scale methods lack semantic selection and parallel instance-level training. We present SemLite-GS, a building-centric framework that reconstructs lightweight building meshes from large-scale UAV oblique imagery. First, an orthographic reference map establishes globally consistent building identities, which are propagated to oblique views to form camera-instance pairs and regions of interest. Second, semantic-selective parallel PGSR training jointly processes multiple pairs within relevant image regions while updating only target Gaussians; contextual Gaussians remain fixed to preserve visibility. Third, architectural planes extracted from rendered depth, opacity, and normal maps guide signed distance field optimization, producing meshes with adaptive polygon allocation and well-defined structural boundaries. Experiments on multiple large-scale UAV datasets demonstrate that our SemLite-GS substantially reduces building reconstruction time compared with representative full-scene 3DGS methods. With comparable polygon budgets, SemLite-GS achieves superior preservation of dominant planar structures and sharp architectural transitions compared with conventional dense reconstruction followed by mesh decimation. The source code is available at https://github.com/IRIS-LAB-whu/SemLite-GS.

Computer Vision.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
Computer Vision.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

Computer Vision.title: When Does an AUROC Comparison Survive a Change in Population Mix?
Computer Vision.summary: Does an AUROC comparison survive a change in the proportions of tasks, populations, or image corruptions? A pooled-AUROC ranking of failure detectors or uncertainty scores describes one particular mix of groups. We study two fixed scores for a common binary target under mixtures of fixed group-conditional laws. Using the cross-group AUC decomposition, we prove that every rational symmetric quadratic comparison geometry is realizable by finite scalar-score distributions. Universal dominance is thus coNP-hard, and even exhaustive checks of every mixture on fewer than $K$ groups can miss a $K$-group reversal. A grid bound gives a dimension-uniform approximation certificate with sharp $1/m$ order. Common score marginals across groups make the comparison numerator linear, with an error envelope for imperfect alignment. These results yield exact finite-bank audits, explicit reversal mixtures and distances, and simultaneous population statements. For failure detection with a frozen ResNet-50 on ImageNet-C, 15 of 18 confidence-score comparisons win in every corruption family on a discovery split, and all 15 are finite-bank certified over all family mixtures on a held-out split; over all 15 corruption types, of 14 discovery winners the corrected grid certifies 10, leaves 3 unresolved, and finds one confirmation reversal of at least 0.05 AUROC. An audit of all 11,019 released Stable LM 2 12B outputs and 35 uncertainty methods finds 66 confirmation-set comparisons that win within all four tasks yet reverse under mixing. Discovery-fitted marginal rank alignment removes all 66; an alignment-error envelope certifies 83 comparisons. Label checks also change several selected reversals. The findings distinguish robustness of frozen scores from robustness after calibration; they do not establish human-error detection, robustness to unseen corruptions, or generalization beyond the evaluated banks.
Computer Vision.comment: 30 pages, 5 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Computer Vision.title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields
Computer Vision.summary: Auroras provide remote optical observations of energetic electrons precipitating into the upper atmosphere, and whose energy distribution encodes key information about large scale magnetospheric processes. Recovering the underlying electron precipitation field from ground-based camera images of auroras remains a challenging inverse problem. Existing auroral tomography techniques are often limited to simplified static settings, discrete spatial and energy grids, or strong assumptions on the electron energy spectrum. We propose to model the dynamic auroral electron precipitation field via a temporally conditioned neural network. The state of the precipitation field at each frame is represented by a per-frame latent code driven by learned discrete dynamics. A shared decoder maps horizontal positions and latent states to electron energy spectra. The predicted flux is converted to multi-wavelength volume emission rates and rendered into camera images accounting for delayed emissions. We evaluate the method on synthetic dynamic auroral sequences and real multi-view auroral videos, showing that the proposed representation produces temporally coherent precipitation reconstructions and image projections consistent with the observations.
Computer Vision.comment: Accepted to the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027). Camera-ready version with supplementary material. 17 pages, 15 figures

Computer Vision.title: Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay for Continual Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation
Computer Vision.summary: Conventional experience replay typically applies fixed preservation constraints to historical exemplars, overlooking variations in how learned representations, predictions, and anatomical structures change during sequential training. To address this limitation, we propose Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay Loss (DCSRL), an exemplar-adaptive supervision mechanism that regulates anatomical preservation according to source-referenced knowledge drift. DCSRL operates within a reliability-guided replay framework that selects informative historical exemplars using anatomical content and boundary characteristics while adaptively regulating replay during training. For each retained exemplar, DCSRL constructs a frozen source-task reference signature and subsequently measures changes in feature representations, class probabilities, boundary responses, and predicted anatomical structures. These complementary drift measurements are aggregated and normalized to generate bounded, exemplar-specific coefficients that dynamically adjust boundary and structural replay losses without modifying the underlying memory-selection policy. We evaluate DCSRL under sequential learning across CAMUS, CardiacNet, and EchoNet-Dynamic, comparing its performance with regularization-, distillation-, and replay-based continual-learning approaches. Experimental findings indicate that DCSRL improves overall final segmentation performance and anatomical boundary preservation, particularly under heterogeneous imaging conditions, although trade-offs remain in knowledge transfer across tasks. These findings suggest that source-referenced multidimensional drift conditioning offers a promising direction for adaptive anatomical knowledge preservation in continual cardiac ultrasound segmentation.

Computer Vision.title: Input-Space versus Feature-Level Conditioning for Robust Facial Expression Recognition
Computer Vision.summary: Facial expression recognition (FER) degrades sharply when illumination, exposure or resolution departs from the training distribution. Two remedies dominate practice: enriching the input signal, or conditioning intermediate features on an estimated image quality. The two are rarely compared under matched backbones, training budgets and condition annotations, and their cost is seldom reported. We present a controlled comparison on RAF-DB. Input-space conditioning uses four deterministic, label-free views (logarithmic stretching, inverse-logarithmic stretching, down-up resampling and identity), each processed by a shared backbone with a branch-specific BatchNorm and linear head, with the branch logits averaged. Feature-space conditioning is implemented as FiLM and Conditional BatchNorm under an identical protocol. Across six backbone architectures the input-space variant improves top-1 accuracy on every one (mean +0.94 percentage points; bootstrap interval [0.51, 1.63]; sign test p = 0.016), with a seed-controlled estimate of +0.42 percentage points on ResNet-18, whereas feature-level conditioning yields +0.10 and +0.03 percentage points. We attribute the gap to the information content of the heuristic condition label rather than to the conditioning mechanism. The gain costs 4.00x FLOPs, 4.18x latency and 3.79x training time, i.e. 0.26 percentage points per additional GFLOP, and we state an explicit rule for when the trade is worth making.

Computer Vision.title: SEAT: Sign-Type Evidence-Audited Transport for Multi-Label Tongue Diagnosis
Computer Vision.summary: Automated tongue-sign recognition can improve the consistency of non-invasive examinations that otherwise rely on subjective visual judgment. A single tongue image often exhibits multiple coexisting signs characterized by heterogeneous evidence, including localized morphology, global chromaticity, and inter-label dependence. However, existing methods typically rely on shared representations and uniform multi-label heads, making it difficult to verify whether predictions stem from clinically relevant evidence rather than spurious visual correlations. We propose SEAT, an evidence-audited framework that matches distinct evidence types with dedicated prediction and evaluation mechanisms. Built on frozen DINOv2 patch features, SEAT couples mask-guided sign-specific attention for localized morphology, a semi-relaxed optimal transport pathway over LAB/HSV color prototypes to enhance pale-tongue recognition, and a co-occurrence-aware transport regularizer to shape the batch-level predicted label marginal. These components are evaluated through audits matched to their evidence types. On the TongueDx benchmark, SEAT achieves a mean macro-F1 of 72.59 with a standard deviation of 1.04 across six random seeds, with a six-model ensemble reaching 74.15. The ensemble outperforms a backbone-matched baseline and a larger, domain-specialized vision-language model by 8.06 and 2.99 percentage points, respectively. Our results demonstrate that aligning dedicated prediction pathways and audits with sign-specific characteristics improves multi-label accuracy while offering more targeted evidential grounding than uniform post-hoc spatial explanations. Code is available at https://github.com/NEU-TCM-Lab/Sign-type-Evidence-Audited-Transport.

Computer Vision.title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
Computer Vision.summary: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. Internal analyses of Vision Transformers reveal patterns consistent with aggregation failure, where object evidence is present at the patch level but not consolidated into the final prediction. Using this characterization as a diagnostic probe, a simple spatial re-ranking strategy recovers a subset of these errors and improves in-sample accuracy by up to 5.7 percentage points. These results establish context sensitivity as a continuous and predictable property of modern vision systems, with Vision Transformer analyses suggesting that aggregation limitations may contribute to some failure types even when object evidence remains available.

Computer Vision.title: Event-based object detection under adverse lighting and motion: lessons for construction sites
Computer Vision.summary: Vision-based monitoring on construction sites fails at night, at dawn and dusk, in tunnels and under floodlights, when conventional RGB cameras under- or over-expose. Event cameras record per-pixel brightness changes with microsecond latency and over 120 dB of dynamic range, but their benefit for site-relevant object detection has not been quantified on real data. We compare three recent event-based detectors (SMamba, SATE and EvRT-DETR) with an RGB detector trained on the same data, using the pixel-aligned PEOD dataset. On low-light frames (70% of the test set) the best event detector reaches 27.2 AP against 21.3 AP for RGB, and a training-free late fusion of both sensors is the best option in every lighting condition (33.3 AP). An object-level analysis of 53,091 objects shows that brightness has little effect on event detectors, whereas fast motion matters: above 20 pixels per frame RGB finds 11-19% of medium-size objects and EvRT-DETR 39-60%. Activation patching locates the damage caused by losing events at the 1/16-resolution features, with small objects depending on the finest scale, and shows that event detectors fail when few signal events meet added noise. A model-agnostic pruning study keeps about 95% of accuracy with 60% of the input but halves small-object recall. On rendered construction sites, used zero-shot, dimming the floodlights drops RGB to near zero while the event detector keeps most of its AP50. We close with camera-placement guidance for construction sites.

Computer Vision.title: Variational Trajectory Optimization of Anisotropic Diffusion Schedules
Computer Vision.summary: We introduce a variational framework for diffusion models with anisotropic noise schedules parameterized by a matrix-valued path $M_t(θ)$ that allocates noise across subspaces. Central to our framework is a trajectory-level objective that jointly trains the score network and \emph{learns} $M_t(θ)$, which encompasses general parameterization classes of matrix-valued noise schedules. We further derive an estimator for $\partial_θ\nabla \log p_t$ that enables efficient optimization of the $M_t(θ)$ schedule. For inference, we develop an efficiently-implementable reverse-ODE solver that is an anisotropic generalization of the second-order Heun discretization algorithm. Across CIFAR-10, AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet-64, our method consistently improves FID with largest gains at low NFE. Code is available at https://github.com/kilonova801/anisotropic-diffusion.

Computer Vision.title: From Cloud to Edge: A Fully Local Pipeline for Pothole Risk Assessment and Driver Warning Generation
Computer Vision.summary: Vision-language models can turn road images into clear, geometry-aware pothole warnings, but current systems depend on commercial cloud services. Our earlier five-stage pipeline needed two cloud calls per scene, taking about 20 s and USD 0.105, and could not run offline. We rebuild every stage to run on a single local GPU and evaluate it with the same data, prompts, and protocol. Segmentation keeps the original Segment Anything weights but runs them in half precision with graph compilation, which makes it 2.7x faster without changing any downstream risk class; five lightweight variants could not match its masks on small road defects. Severity is graded by six ConvNeXt students distilled from 3092 cloud labels. They reach Cohen's kappa = 0.268 against human consensus at 28 ms per pothole, close to the cloud model's 0.321, within the camera setup they were trained for. A local 8-billion-parameter vision-language model writes the warnings under a grammar that admits only in-lane maneuvers. Three blind, independent raters scored these warnings safer than the cloud warnings (4.18 vs. 3.65 of 5; p = 0.001; 50 scenes) and equally clear, whereas an automated LLM judge ranked them the other way. The complete pipeline runs at 1.27 s per scene, 16x faster than the cloud system, offline and at no per-scene cost.
Computer Vision.comment: 23 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables. And submitted to MDPI Sensors

Computer Vision.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
Computer Vision.summary: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. Cross-cycle caches such as C$^3$ache reuse computation from earlier replanning calls, but whether they beat simply taking fewer steps is unclear. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. Two uncached steps keep the success of ten: on all 500 initial states they are non-inferior within two percentage points, for one checkpoint and noise seed. Under PyTorch's default compile mode, they also cut a replanning call on an RTX A6000 from 202 to 92 ms. This leaves little room for caching. A cache that keeps two fresh steps cannot be faster than two uncached steps: every call still encodes the images, runs the video expert and computes those two steps. Caching the first of two steps, refreshed every fourth call, saves at most 11--14% of a call by our cost model. Cached policies are also fragile. Their losses tracked the share of the flow path the cached steps cover: under Fast-WAM's current time shift, C$^3$ache's eight cached steps cover 80% of the path instead of 44%, and the cached policy succeeds on 63% of states against 95% uncached. Resampling the noise on every call cost caches covering 60% or more of the path 14--40 points. These results argue for fewer-step baselines and for testing reuse under the deployed sampler and noise settings. We release our evaluation harness, logs and a checklist.
Computer Vision.comment: Honorable Mention at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Efficient Foundation Models for Real-Time Embodied AI (EEAI). Code and data available at https://github.com/gabhinav001/cache-or-denoise-less

Computer Vision.title: Edge-Adaptive Hiera-Seg Model for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
Computer Vision.summary: Building integrated photovoltaic power forecasting is challenging because facade orientation, rooftop geometry, nearby buildings, vegetation, cloud movement, module temperature, inverter status and edge device reliability jointly affect power generation. This paper proposes an edge-adaptive HieraSeg model for short term BIPV power forecasting with multi-orientation visual-irradiance fusion. RGB facade images, optional thermal cues, irradiance measurements, module temperature, facade orientation, rooftop masks, shading labels, sky condition, historical power and edge device state are aligned into synchronous forecasting windows. HieraSeg extracts hierarchical regions from facade, rooftop, sky, shadow and background images, while the edge-adaptive module changes feature weights under missing frames, latency shifts and local shading changes. The segmentation branch identifies occluded module areas and separates facade, rooftop, sky and background evidence before the forecasting head estimates future BIPV output. Experiments are designed on a simulated multibuilding BIPV dataset with unseen building and unseen orientation tests. The model reports predicted power, confidence interval, dominant evidence, occlusion contribution, orientation contribution and energy-management review priority. This output is intended to show whether the forecast is driven by irradiance change, visible shading, orientation response, stale edge information or recent power history. The framework supports local forecasting at edge controllers with limited communication delay and computing resources, linking visual occlusion, irradiance dynamics and power history to traceable forecasting results for building energy management, microgrid scheduling and BIPV operation planning.

Computer Vision.title: Adversarial Attacks Expose Path-Dependent Failures in Discrete Medical Image Tokenizers
Computer Vision.summary: Discrete image tokenizers convert medical images into token sequences that downstream models either decode into an image for a classifier (the reconstruction path), classify directly (the token path), or feed to a generative multimodal model. We ask whether imperceptible input perturbations can break these systems through the tokenizer alone. We evaluate four tokenizers on three imaging modalities and extend the strongest attack to a deployed generative model. Our central finding is path-dependence: the same tokenizer fails in opposite ways depending on how its output is used. A supervised attack collapses diagnostic accuracy on the reconstruction path, with ROC AUC falling to $\leq 0.013$ at $ε=2/255$ on all four tokenizers, while sparing the token path. An unsupervised, label-free attack does the reverse; its damage concentrates in the multi-codebook tokenizers, worst in MedITok, whose token-path AUC falls from 0.919 to 0.239. The same label-free attack transfers to LLaVA-Med, a frozen medical vision-language model built on MedITok, making it report proliferative diabetic retinopathy in a healthy retina or call a malignant lesion benign, without access to the question, answer, or language-model gradients. Harm is driven by how far the attack moves the tokenizer's internal representation, not by how many tokens change: on the learned-codebook tokenizers, a control attack that changes nearly all tokens but moves the representation less leaves every path and answer intact. Domain-specific pretraining does not provide robustness: MedITok has the best clean accuracy yet is the most fragile, more so than UniTok, its general-domain counterpart. None of six candidate defenses repairs every failure mode, and several fail once the attacker optimizes against the defense directly. Medical tokenizer robustness must therefore be evaluated per downstream path, against an adaptive adversary.
Computer Vision.comment: 21 pages, 9 figures, 18 tables. Accepted at the GenAI4Health Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026, Sydney

Artificial Intelligence.title: Where Polanyi Meets Galois: Tacit Knowing as an Algebro-Deterministic Operation, Toward Re-rooting AI-Generated Science
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Tacit knowing is an operating regime of memory, not a separate content. In VaCoAl (CASRAM, PyVaCoAl), a deterministic hyperdimensional memory over GF(2), one DAG of bound records is read in two ways. With all collisions repaired (Rescue), the trace is exactly auditable but no path outranks any; with collisions tolerated (Don't Care), a path confidence $CR_2$ ranks direct over circuitous routes unstated. This audit-valuation complementarity formalizes Polanyi's claim that tacit and explicit are not sharply divided. (1) Polanyi's from-to is non-commutative binding. (2) Full explication destroys the valuation (Lemma 1), as with Polanyi's pianist; tacitness is contingent or regime-bound, putting Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins on one substrate. (3) The lemma answers the popular dual-process moral ("train slow System 2 to tame fast System 1"), mirroring the two-store reading of knowledge Polanyi rejected; Mercier and Sperber's reasoning as intuitive inference about reasons matches his. (4) To know a large DAG is to cull it. Against Polanyi's Meno reading, Simon held that a test and a generator, guided by statable heuristics, suffice. The AlphaGo-to-AlphaProof lineage builds the test, but its strongest systems cull by unstatable valuations: the tacit is relocated, not removed, results are verified yet rootless, and practicable traces must record the cull. (5) Collins's three tacit knowledges are bound structure, substrate valuation and value binding. (6) Our mentor-student DAG maps tacit transmission. (7) AI-solved problems lacking follow-ups (Tao) are rootless explicit knowledge, re-rooted if LLMs generate, VaCoAl traces, the community values. (8) For Mercier and Sperber an LLM is a sophist; truth-seeking lies in collective tacit knowing, Polanyi's conviviality, conjectured to extend beyond humans; machine-only knowledge reaches at most Sosa's animal grade. Testable predictions follow.

Artificial Intelligence.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Beyond Answering: Learning to Speak First and Act in Streaming Video
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in the evolving visual stream and initiate conversations at appropriate moments without a user query. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC) lets the model act on what it sees by invoking external tools using the current visual and conversational context and incorporating returned information into the ongoing interaction. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) supports visual grounding in both user inputs and model outputs. The model can identify objects marked by users on video frames and produce frame-aligned bounding boxes to link its responses to specific objects and regions. To develop these capabilities, we construct a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and adopt a three-stage training scheme to integrate the new behaviors with AURA's existing streaming interaction abilities. We further incorporate Long-Horizon Interaction Memory (LHIM) to maintain contextual continuity over extended video streams. Evaluations on public streaming benchmarks show that AURA 2.0 achieves leading performance among open-source streaming models, while targeted evaluations further validate its new interaction capabilities.

Artificial Intelligence.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention. We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair. We evaluate controllable generation and localized repair on these datasets, respectively, and assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 21 pages. Revised the human evaluation protocol, clarified the generation task-success and repair pass-vote metrics, and updated Table 1 and the appendix

Artificial Intelligence.title: From Data to Wisdom: Rethinking AI Through an Epistemic Lens
Artificial Intelligence.summary: This paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture for AI (EAAI), a conceptual framework treating Data, Information, Knowledge, Understanding and Wisdom as five distinct but recursively interacting epistemic functions: observation, contextual interpretation, modeling and prediction, critical evaluation and informed judgment. Two observations motivate it: sequential readings of the Knowledge Pyramid obscure how these functions interact, and a targeted review of twelve Bayesian reference books finds that prior distributions are defined mathematically while "prior information" and "prior knowledge" are not consistently distinguished as epistemic categories. A Bayesian interpretation relates the likelihood, prior and posterior distributions, posterior prediction, model checking and decision analysis to the five functions, without limiting EAAI to Bayesian systems. Extending "prior" in an epistemic sense, the paper distinguishes five kinds of prior context that can shape the model, the likelihood, the prior, evaluation and action. Three worked applications -- quantitative financial risk, actuarial modeling in health insurance and agentic AI for medical reimbursement claims -- show how EAAI structures the analysis of model assumptions, evidence interpretation, validation, dependencies and decision consequences, separating the prediction of a risk, the appraisal of its reliability and the justification of action. It draws implications for AI and machine learning, including evaluation by function, treating intermediate model outputs as evidence open to challenge and separating generation from appraisal, and compares EAAI with work on DIKW, Bayesian workflow, AI evaluation and risk governance. Its contributions are an epistemic vocabulary with recursive relationships, a more accessible reading of Bayesian methodology, a typology of prior context and clearer methodological terminology
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 27 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. v2: review extended to twelve books (Berger 1985; Kochenderfer et al. 2022); new Appendix A with editions, quoted passages and term counts; likelihood split into data model (Knowledge) and likelihood at the observed data (Information); Figure 3 now four findings and one implication

Artificial Intelligence.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$) CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent optimal of the same output is polylogarithmic in $n$, specifically at most $O(\log^9{n})$. This is remarkable, as it shows an exponential speedup by switching to CGP. Our results shed light on the benefit and the compactness of the graph-based representation for programs, and on how CGP can navigate its search and fitness spaces efficiently. This is a first proven performance guarantee for CGP on an established benchmark problem. Experiments complement our theoretical findings.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: Accepted as a poster at NeurIPS 2026. To appear in the conference proceedings

Artificial Intelligence.title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Languages of India need 1.6 to 14 times as many tokens as English on GPT-4o's tokenizer for the same content, which makes them more expensive and slower to serve. We train tokenizers from scratch on human-written text in about 200 languages. Havon v3 is a byte-level BPE tokenizer with 262,144 tokens and a pre-tokenizer that keeps combining marks with their letters and chunks scripts written without spaces. On FLORES-200 devtest it needs fewer tokens than GPT-4o's o200k_base on all 25 languages of India (median 0.74 of GPT-4o's count) and on 172 of 204 languages, but 7% more on English. Havon v4 adds a second, multi-word training stage (SuperBPE) to v3. At exactly GPT-4o's vocabulary size of 200,019 tokens, v4 needs 6.1% fewer tokens than GPT-4o on English and fewer on 161 of 204 languages and all 25 languages of India (median 0.74); at the same size, v3 needs 9.4% more on English and wins on 133. With 262,144 tokens, v4 needs 9.6% fewer tokens on English and fewer on 182 of 204 languages, and with 524,288 tokens it needs fewer on 203 of 204. The gains are largest for English, Hindi and the Romance languages; scripts without spaces, such as Khmer, Burmese and Tibetan, gain little and lose subword merges. Havon v5 replaces v4's Python-only code sample with permissively licensed code in 15 languages: on code it needs 1.03 to 1.22 times GPT-4o's tokens, against 1.11 to 1.29 for v4, while keeping all 25 languages of India (median 0.74, all significant under a sentence-level bootstrap) and English (0.94). These are compression results only: we have not yet evaluated a model trained with v4 or v5.

Artificial Intelligence.title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Commercial language model APIs bill per token, so a tokenizer that needs more tokens for the same content in one language makes that language more expensive, slower, and able to fit less text in a fixed context window. We measure this disparity for nine public tokenizers, including those of GPT-4, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5, DeepSeek-V3, Mistral-Nemo and four Sarvam models, on all 25 languages of India available in FLORES-200 (2,009 professionally translated sentences aligned with English) and on 13,732 human-translated Hinglish-English social media pairs from PHINC. On GPT-4o's tokenizer the same content needs between 1.57 times (Hindi) and 5.01 times (Odia) the tokens of English, and 13.7 times for Santali in Ol Chiki script; GPT-4's tokenizer needs up to 12.8 times. Sarvam-30B/105B is the only third-party tokenizer that stays below 2.6 times on every language (median 1.53). In an illustrative scenario using official list prices accessed on 5 November 2026 and stated assumptions, a support bot handling 100,000 chats a month on GPT-4o would cost about INR 56,640 in English and INR 102,829 in Marathi; these are estimates, not measured production costs. Against an openly licensed Hindi and Marathi morphological segmentation set, no tokenizer places more than 35% of its word-internal boundaries on morpheme boundaries (boundary F1 at most 0.48). In a companion paper we present a tokenizer that reduces this tax. Code, pinned artifacts and raw token counts are available at https://github.com/HavonAI/indic-token-tax.

Artificial Intelligence.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
Artificial Intelligence.summary: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Dantzig--Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying constraint families, and each candidate costs a column generation run. The choice is hard when families strengthen the bound only together, as in classical lot-sizing, network-design, and facility-location formulations. We prove that when an evaluation convexifies at most $s$ of $k$ families, methods that observe only bounds need of order $k^w$ evaluations to find a hidden group of $w$ families in the worst case. A prediction missing $e$ members reduces this to $Θ(k^e)$ through a staged search that need not know $e$. The orders extend to several groups, prices, and growing evaluation costs. We study two predictors: a lookahead at an optimal LP dual, which vanishes on groups whose families share no variable, and language models reading the model, verified by the staged search in JointDW. Such groups appear in three of ten MIPLIB-NL models whose bound can be improved and in all 59 benchmark instances. Given the coefficients of constructed models with up to 16 families, one language model names a true group first in 249 of 252 answers. On the benchmark instances, decompositions chosen by language models from the text solve faster than those of GCG's detector.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 69 pages, 5 figures, 31 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/junbolian/JointDW

Artificial Intelligence.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Formal verification using proof assistants provides strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing proofs remains labor-intensive and requires significant expertise. Recent approaches based on large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating proof synthesis. However, these approaches typically constrain the model to a rigid tactic-generation loop, in which the surrounding system controls premise retrieval, proof-state management, and backtracking. We introduce ProofCoder, an agentic proof-synthesis system for Rocq that approaches theorem proving from a coding-agent perspective. Rather than generating tactics within a fixed loop, ProofCoder reasons continuously throughout proof search and uses proof-assistant feedback to decide when to gather additional information, inspect proof states, revise previously generated proof fragments, or backtrack to an earlier point in the proof. This allows it to iteratively construct, repair, and refine proofs, at either tactic-level or whole-proof granularity. We evaluate ProofCoder on 280 challenging verification tasks from the AutoRocq Benchmark. On the best-performing configurations, ProofCoder increases proof success from 47% to 60% over the state-of-theart AutoRocq system, corresponding to a 27.7% relative improvement at approximately half the cost. Our ablations identify continuous reasoning as a key design choice: without it, the agent solves fewer lemmas at substantially higher cost, backtracks four to six times more often, and more frequently discards its own revisions. Whole-proof and tactic-level generation achieve similar success rates but follow distinct search and repair strategies. These results suggest that effective automated software verification requires more than improved tactic selection: continuous reasoning and feedback-guided proof revision are critical ingredients for robust proof synthesis.

Artificial Intelligence.title: AAC: Admissible-by-Architecture Differentiable Landmark Compression for ALT
Artificial Intelligence.summary: We introduce the Architecturally Admissible Compressor (AAC), which adapts landmark-based A* heuristics to query demand under a fixed label-memory budget. AAC provides two continuous relaxations of ALT (A*, Landmarks, and Triangle inequality) selection. With exact landmark distances, every parameter value defines a lower bound on shortest-path distance. Both relaxations deploy ALT using only the selected labels. The row-stochastic relaxation takes convex combinations of landmark distances. We characterize the maximal admissibility-preserving linear classes and prove that the relaxed and discrete optima coincide. The fractional relaxation mixes subset heuristics and supports continuous greedy (AAC-CG) with exact gradients and an entropy-regularized oracle for differentiable selection. For expected heuristic value, we prove an approximation guarantee with finite-step, oracle-error, and finite-sample terms. The limiting $1-1/e$ factor is optimal for arbitrary supplied pools and query distributions unless P${=}$NP. At matched label memory, AAC-CG reduces A* expansions by $1.9$-$22.7$% relative to farthest-point ALT (FPS-ALT) in all $19$ tested combinations of graph and memory budget across six road networks and two synthetic graphs. Each combination uses one $500$-query test split; all methods share distance tables when distances are symmetric. Canonical greedy also expands fewer nodes than FPS-ALT in all $19$ graph-budget pairs. AAC-CG achieves $99.6$% of canonical greedy's mean heuristic value on test queries, averaged over these pairs. AAC makes admissibility independent of training success, while its analysis and experiments distinguish selection quality from search efficiency.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 80 pages. Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) with Reproducibility Certification. Code: https://github.com/anindex/aac

Artificial Intelligence.title: CardioLM: A multilingual suite of small language models for the cardiology domain
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Background: Cardiovascular care generates large volumes of clinical free-text documentation in local languages. However, clinical natural language processing (NLP) resources remain concentrated in English, and no existing benchmark is cardiology-specific, multilingual, and broad in entity coverage. Methods: We present two contributions. The first is CardioCCC, a corpus of 508 cardiology case reports originally published in Spanish and extended to Czech, Dutch, English, Italian, Romanian, and Swedish through machine translation, annotation projection, and clinician review, with annotations covering diseases, symptoms, procedures, and medications. The second is CardioLM, comprising CardioBERTa, a set of language-specific encoders obtained by continued pretraining on cardiology and biomedical corpora, and CardioNER, a set of named entity recognition (NER) models fine-tuned on CardioCCC. Results: Cardiology-specific pretraining reduced pseudo-perplexity by up to a factor of eight, yet changed strict span-level F1 by at most 0.04, with benefits concentrated in languages whose backbones lacked biomedical coverage. The jointly trained multilingual XLM-RoBERTa-large models achieved the best strict F1 in nearly every language and entity type, exceeding the strongest monolingual system by up to 0.13 F1. A large share of residual errors concerned boundary detection: relaxed matching recovered 0.10-0.23 F1 for disease, procedure, and symptom, but only 0.01-0.07 for medication. Clinicians rated CardioNER well above a rule- and dictionary-based baseline, with the mean rating across entity types rising from 26% to 73%. Conclusions: Specialty-specific pretraining is not the decisive factor for downstream entity recognition, whereas multilingual joint training yields the strongest results in nearly all settings and a simpler deployment path for multi-country clinical information extraction.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 89 pages, 7 figures, 33 tables (9 in the main text, 23 in Appendix A, and 1 in Appendix B)

Artificial Intelligence.title: FisherDistill: Diffusion Distribution Distillation via Closed-Form Fisher Critics
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Recent advances in diffusion distillation have enabled high-quality image generation in only one or a few network function evaluations (NFEs). Despite their efficiency, aggressively distilled generators often retain a residual distribution gap from their multi-step teachers, motivating recent methods to introduce adversarial refinement with a learned discriminator. In this work, we ask whether such refinement necessarily requires a learned adversarial discriminator. We introduce \textbf{FisherDistill}, a simple alternative based on Fisher linear discriminant analysis. Using intermediate representations from the frozen teacher, we estimate the first- and second-order statistics of real and generated samples and derive a closed-form Fisher direction that maximally separates their feature distributions relative to within-class variation. This direction provides a lightweight refinement signal that complements the original distillation objective without requiring an additional adversarial discriminator or its optimization loop. Across multiple distillation frameworks, our approach consistently improves generation quality over their respective distilled baselines and substantially closes the gap to adversarially refined counterparts. Code: https://bhosalems.github.io/FisherDistill/

Artificial Intelligence.title: Feedback Forensics: A Toolkit to Measure AI Personality
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Some traits making a "good" AI model are hard to describe upfront. For example, should responses be more polite or more casual? Such traits are sometimes summarized as model character or personality. Without a clear objective, conventional benchmarks based on automatic checks struggle to measure such traits. Evaluation methods using human feedback such as Chatbot Arena have emerged as a popular alternative.
